output_json.patch_notes: In IOUtils.unzip(String, String): compute destDirCanonicalPath = new File(extractFolder).getCanonicalPath() once. For each ZipEntry, after building destFile = new File(newPath, currentEntry), compute destFile.getCanonicalPath() and verify it equals destDirCanonicalPath or starts with destDirCanonicalPath + File.separator; otherwise throw IOException("Zip entry is outside of the target dir: " + currentEntry) before calling destinationParent.mkdirs() or opening the FileOutputStream. This check runs for every entry (files and directories alike) so directory-only traversal entries are also blocked before mkdirs(). Added IOUtilsUnzipTest.java with JUnit 4 tests: rejects "../pov_zipslip_proof.txt", rejects nested "../../evil.txt", rejects a directory-only traversal entry "../evildir/", and confirms a normal nested entry ("safe/nested/file.txt") still extracts correctly.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only adds a containment check before existing filesystem operations; it does not alter behavior for well-formed archives whose entries stay within the extraction root (verified via a passing "still extracts normal entries" test and the full existing module test suite, 9/9 passing). getCanonicalPath() can throw IOException on some platforms/filesystem edge cases (e.g. broken symlinks) — this is already declared by unzip()'s throws clause so no new checked-exception surface is introduced. Absolute-path zip entries were analyzed and, per java.io.UnixFileSystem's resolve() semantics (parent+child concatenation, not replacement), remain naturally contained under the extraction root on this JDK/OS combination, and are additionally covered by the canonical-path check regardless. Symlink-based escapes are also mitigated since getCanonicalPath() resolves symlinks before the comparison.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) in IOUtils.unzip(). Untrusted ZipEntry names were used to build destFile via new File(newPath, currentEntry) without any containment check, allowing entries like "../pov_zipslip_proof.txt" to create directories (destinationParent.mkdirs()) and write files (new FileOutputStream(destFile)) outside the intended extraction folder. The fix canonicalizes the extraction root once and, for every entry, canonicalizes the resolved destFile and rejects (throws IOException) any entry whose canonical path is not equal to or a descendant of the canonical extraction root — before any mkdirs() or file write occurs. This single check at the shared trust boundary covers both sink operations (parent directory creation and file write) and blocks the standard bypass variants (simple/nested "../" traversal, directory-only traversal entries) since it operates on the fully resolved/normalized path rather than naive string matching.
